request: why should a solar panel face the sun directly?

beats.intent: A solar panel square-on to eight parallel sunbeams, all eight hitting it
beats.narration: Face a panel straight at the Sun and it catches every beam across its width.
beats.code:
stage.title("Tilting a solar panel")
panel = Line([1, -1.5, 0], [1, 1.5, 0], color=BLUE, stroke_width=10)
stage.play(Create(panel))
stage.add(panel)
ys = np.linspace(-1.3125, 1.3125, 8)
beams = [Arrow([-5, y, 0], [0.9, y, 0], buff=0, color=YELLOW) for y in ys]
stage.play(*[GrowArrow(b) for b in beams])
stage.add(*beams)
stage.caption("square on: all 8 beams")

beats.intent: The panel tilted 60°: only the middle 4 beams reach it, the outer 4 pass by dimmed
beats.narration: Tilt it sixty degrees and it presents a narrower target: now only four of the eight beams land on it.
beats.code:
stage.play(Rotate(panel, 60 * DEGREES, about_point=[1, 0, 0]))
hit = [abs(y) < 0.75 for y in ys]
stage.play(*[b.animate.put_start_and_end_on([-5, y, 0], [1 - np.sqrt(3) * y - 0.05, y, 0]) if h else b.animate.set_opacity(0.2)
             for b, y, h in zip(beams, ys, hit)])
stage.caption("tilted 60°: 4 of 8 beams")

beats.intent: The tilted panel beside power ∝ cos 60° = 0.5
beats.narration: The share of light it catches is the cosine of the tilt: cos sixty is a half.

request: how do I work out a 15% tip on a £40 bill?

beats.intent: A bar of 40 split into ten parts of £4
beats.narration: Split the bill into ten equal parts: each is ten percent, four pounds.
beats.code:
stage.title("A 15% tip")
bar = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=1.0, height=0.8, color=WHITE, fill_color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3) for _ in range(10)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).move_to([0, 0.4, 0])
stage.play(Create(bar))
stage.add(bar)
stage.label(bar, "£40", direction=UP)
stage.label(bar[0], "£4", direction=DOWN, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: One part lit for 10% and half of the next for 5%
beats.narration: Ten percent is four pounds. Five percent is half of that: two pounds.
beats.code:
stage.play(bar[0].animate.set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.8))
half = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=0.8, stroke_width=0, fill_color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to(bar[1].get_center() + 0.25 * LEFT)
stage.play(FadeIn(half))
stage.add(half)
stage.caption("10% = £4, 5% = £2")

beats.narration: Together, fifteen percent is six pounds.

request: how does a binary search tree find a number?

beats.intent: A tree with 8 at the root, 3 and 10 below, then 1, 6 and 14
beats.narration: In a binary search tree, smaller numbers go left and bigger ones go right.

beats.intent: The path 8 → 3 → 6 lit as the search for 6
beats.narration: To find six: six is less than eight, go left. Six is more than three, go right. Found it.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, dots["8"], color=YELLOW)
stage.play(links[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW).set_stroke(width=6))
highlight(stage, dots["3"], color=YELLOW)
stage.play(links[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW).set_stroke(width=6))
highlight(stage, dots["6"], color=GREEN)
stage.caption("6 < 8: left.  6 > 3: right.")

beats.intent: The tree beside: 3 looks for 6 numbers, about log₂ n in a balanced tree
beats.narration: Each step throws away half the tree, so a balanced tree of a million numbers needs only about twenty steps.

request: how far is a light year?

beats.intent: A beam of light travelling from a dot, one second marked as 300 000 km
beats.narration: Light travels three hundred thousand kilometres every second, seven and a half times round the Earth.
beats.code:
stage.title("A light year")
src = Dot([-5.5, 0, 0], color=YELLOW, radius=0.14)
stage.play(GrowFromCenter(src))
stage.add(src)
beam = Arrow([-5.5, 0, 0], [-3.5, 0, 0], buff=0, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(GrowArrow(beam))
stage.add(beam)
stage.label(beam, "1 s: 300 000 km", direction=UP, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: A second, far longer beam below it, labelled 1 year
beats.narration: Keep it going for a whole year: about thirty one and a half million seconds.
beats.code:
year = Arrow([-5.5, -1.0, 0], [5.5, -1.0, 0], buff=0, color=ORANGE)
stage.play(GrowArrow(year), run_time=2)
stage.add(year)
stage.label(year, "1 year of travel", direction=DOWN, color=ORANGE)

beats.narration: Three hundred thousand times thirty one and a half million is about nine and a half trillion kilometres: one light year.
